T o bridge this gap, we introduce the Multi-Objective State-Action Network (MOSAN), an
autonomous cognitive information-fusion framework specifically designed for long-horizon scientific
experimentation and sensor shift adaptation. MOSAN was initially validated on the challenging task
of SERS-based bacterial classification. At its core, the framework integrates an Organic Strategic Graph
Memory (OSGM), a persistent directed multigraph that enables principled cross-campaign knowledge
fusion. In this graph, nodes encode experimental states and edges represent tool executions weighted
by multi-objective impact vectors, with Q-values dynamically propagated via the Bellman optimality
equation.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The final SERS architecture was retrained from scratch and evaluated once on an air-gapped Lockbox holdout (mean 87.4% across five seeds), and the ECG5000 transfer was assessed on an unseen 1000-sample holdout (99.3%).
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: One-time terminal evaluation on the zero-knowledge Lockbox holdout for SERS and an isolated 1000-sample holdout for ECG5000.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Cross-validation accuracy and internal variance on the AutoML optimization pool drove Q-value updates and agent decisions.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims of effective sample efficiency, cross-campaign knowledge reuse, and resistance to context degradation are well aligned with reported ablation trajectories, Lockbox test results (87.4% on unseen holdout), and cross-domain ECG5000 performance (0.9930 accuracy).
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluation includes a controlled ablation study isolating deductive reasoning from Optuna Bayesian search, an air-gapped zero-knowledge Lockbox evaluation on SERS bacterial data, zero-shot transfer to the ECG5000 benchmark, and cross-session adaptation on a six-month-aged sensor dataset.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Objective held-out accuracy on the strictly air-gapped Lockbox test set across five random seeds (mean 87.4%) and an unseen 1000-sample ECG5000 test set (99.3%).
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: One-time terminal evaluation of the retrained discovered architecture on an isolated zero-knowledge Lockbox holdout set, and an unseen holdout partition on ECG5000.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Cross-validation accuracy and internal variance computed exclusively on the AutoML optimization training pool guided Q-value updates and agent decisions.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly report substantial GPU computation requirements (91 GPU-hours for SERS), acknowledge validation primarily spanning 1D-to-2D spectral/temporal modalities, and clarify that aged-sensor results serve as a temporal proof-of-concept rather than universal cross-instrument calibration.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is described in detail, including graph state definitions, Bellman Q-value updates, ephemeral cross-domain ghost node injection, decoupled Celery execution, and a strict phased markdown ledger communication mechanism.
primary.quality_rationale: The work presents a thorough architectural design, clear mathematical formulation of the memory graph, robust isolation protocols to prevent data leakage during autonomous optimization, and meaningful empirical comparisons and ablations across multiple campaigns and hardware setups.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces MOSAN, an autonomous multi-agent AutoML framework combining a Single Ledger Architecture, an Organic Strategic Graph Memory with ghost-node seeding, and semantic retrieval to mitigate context dilution and inter-campaign amnesia during spectroscopic and sequential time-series model discovery.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The work presents a thorough architectural design, clear mathematical formulation of the memory graph, robust isolation protocols to prevent data leakage during autonomous optimization, and meaningful empirical comparisons and ablations across multiple campaigns and hardware setups.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly report substantial GPU computation requirements (91 GPU-hours for SERS), acknowledge validation primarily spanning 1D-to-2D spectral/temporal modalities, and clarify that aged-sensor results serve as a temporal proof-of-concept rather than universal cross-instrument calibration.
